items.note: Association name, 1889, Larrow Green, Gideon Vose, creamery 1891 all in Story 1.
Payment by butterfat test not weight is stated, but the second bolded element, 'the test of the station where he delivers governs', is absent.
'made test accuracy a direct financial matter for every patron'.
Loomis, Teague, Sill not named in Section A.
Selby named as Gideon's son but 'taken office in 1911' (key 1913; planted error).
Station-gain line described at 5.25% carried to general account, but the run inverts its shape ('as if milk somehow shed a quarter of its butterfat on the journey') and gives no 1898 origin.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, opened May 4, 1896 (borrowed glass not mentioned in A; core fact present).
No weighing, composite sample or fixed-charge/percent-neck workflow described in A.
Ammon & Sons at Tarnet; outfit arrived 1 May 1897 and put into use (invoice date missing from A, core fact present).
Six dozen pipettes 17.6 cc, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93.
'every month, every season... the figure remained 0.19... June's flush as in February's depth'.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Twenty-nine seasons; dismissed April 30, 1925.
Test book in Keddie's own hand.
3.61 given, but the 1896 figure of 3.80 is never stated in A; both are required.
Nine weeks in May 1911 until July 10, tests higher and then fell back, question mark set.
Married to Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant.
Circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement is absent; both are required.
Died 1934 with the imputation on him.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Brant's the largest.
Weigh book mentioned, but no 1 Jan 1897 start and no statement that the scales agreed.
States Larrow Green 3.78 vs Hollow 3.61 as 'a shortfall of 0.19'. The key's gate on the conflated gap forfeits the item.
Says the committee 'sampled the Hessel Bottom herds through 1908' (key: Jan-Mar only; planted error).
Brant's 1910 200,000 lb / 3.42 and the proportional loss are absent from A.
Custody to Roy Brant and the loan to Ivy are absent.
Alder Corners absent from Section A.
Absent.
Absent.
Absent.
Absent.
Rosalie Cudd absent.
Strawn named and unrelated, but visits 'from 1908 forward' (key 1907-1936; planted error).
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
June 1923, burette, condemned the whole lot (day not given in A).
Says he drew no inference, but attributes a measured figure (16.27 cc) to him and says his notebook 'showed how much the glass cost the patrons'. That contradicts 'wrote no figure'.
1924 average given as 3.85 (key 3.80; planted error).
Loft present, but the notebooks' route to the college library in 1947 is absent; both are required.
Petition January 1925.
Frick, from March 17, two sessions in weigh room, but hearings 'continued through April 4' (key 17 March - 4 May).
Three explanations (water, tester theft, wet hay) heard, and no cause established.
Four books incl. Strawn's condemnation-year notebook, and nobody compared them.
Dismissed April 30, 1925 beside an award of $3,800 'without admission' that found nothing.
Loss given as $19,600 (planted); no one-fifth and no charge to the station-gain account.
Granddaughter, graduate student at State Agricultural College at Farland, with Vaught.
No account of her assembling the separate record series.
February 1958, loft over the station's intake room, nine intact.
16.27 cc (planted NT-1) instead of 16.72.
No 95 percent / 3.80 true test stated in A.
40M lb given, but no 76,000 lb, money given as $19,600, and no ledger identity.
Bulletin 471, October 1958, 33 years after dismissal, 24 after death.
Granddaughter.
Derived via Duncan, Ansel's son.
Second cousins with correct derivation.

Gideon Vose, father.

Treats Duncan's denial as settling the question instead of noting that a family denial is not a record.
True 3.905, short 0.295 (also a 0.21-0.30 range).
960 lb (true test 3.90) instead of 7,200 / 360 lb.
$240 at 25 cents instead of $86.40.
75,310 lb, 5.2% of credited; no 76,000 and no 5.00%/5.26% pair.

26 years 6 weeks correct, but full delivery years given as 26, not 25 (1898-1922).

Variable is the pipette (own vs borrowed), May 8 to July 10.
Same tester, acid, hand tester, herds, season, scales.
Only 'markedly higher' and 'fell back'. The figures 3.80 and 3.61 are never given.
Says the cause is the glass, not milk, tester or feed; the limit given is that it does not show how much the glass was short.
Only one valid reason (1911 interval). Family incentive and posthumous praise are not valid reasons.
No independent valid set; the reason offered as surviving without the 1958 measurement is the invalid family-incentive one.
Abstention A09 asserted: 'So no, there is no evidence Teague questioned the entries', adopting Kyle's pole and ignoring Teague's 1916 claim.
Answers yes and cites the 1919 water circular.
Only two of the five valid points (ledger signatures, 1919 circular); manager date given as 1911.
Abstention A03 asserted: headline 'Almost certainly yes' rests on the station-gain signatures, and the conclusion says he 'probably did not know the tests themselves were faulty'.
Kyle's 1 May 1898 rejected for 1897 on the invoice and diary (NT-10, one carrier only, so E-a).
$3,500 (Cleve) rejected for $3,800 on the office record (NT-9, one carrier only).
First cousin once removed (Cleve) rejected for second cousins on Duncan's record (NT-19, one carrier only).

A06 not addressed.
A10 not addressed.

Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer.
Theft defeated by the 1911 interval with the same tester.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter / nothing summer vs 0.19 in July.

'The sources do not establish what Ansel privately believed was the cause.'
Summary is roughly 200 words, over the 150 cap.
Record series given generically (ledgers, weigh books, test books, diaries, reports, circulars, glass); fewer than five of the keyed nine are identifiable.
Contains 16.27 cc and $19,600.
